preamble: Every clue contains a misprint of one letter in its definition part. The correct letters, read in clue order, spell out a quotation in the Oxford Dictionary of Quotations 4/e (1992). Competitors should submit with their entries a clue like the rest to the fifth word in the quotation (9 letters). NB Preference will be given to clues in which the misprinted and the correct versions make some sense.

messages.text: THE WHOLE SET A CHARACTER DEAD AT EVERY WORD

solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: One regularly making latkes saving bit of stuff in palm

parts.note: saving in the sense 'except' is the same as bar

indicators.note: in places the first letter of stuff inside the palm's name

parts.note: the ita is a South American palm, a crossword favourite

indicators.note: a bit of stuff here is just its opening letter

explanation.surface: Someone who keeps frying potato pancakes squirrels away scraps of material inside their hand.
explanation.walkthrough: The misprint: latkes should read lattes, giving T. 'bit of' supplies S, which goes 'in' ITA.
explanation.definitionFit: A coffee-bar worker is the one who regularly makes lattes and other espresso drinks.

clue.text: Frow, German, coming in stripped

indicators.note: the German letter enters the word for stripped

parts.note: stripped means bare

explanation.surface: A Dutch woman, a German, entering naked.
explanation.walkthrough: The misprint: Frow should read Trow, giving T. A trow is a flat-bottomed river vessel of the Severn.
explanation.definitionFit: A trow is a type of flat-bottomed cargo vessel, so the two are the same kind of craft.

clue.text: To exist within what could be arguable, cried with no rational basis

indicators.note: the verb for exist sits inside the rearranged letters
says arguable could become a different arrangement of its letters

parts.note: to exist is to be

explanation.surface: Someone who wailed, though their case was debatable, had no grounds.
explanation.walkthrough: The misprint: cried should read creed, giving E.
explanation.definitionFit: A German loanword for superstition, a belief held without any reasoned grounds.

clue.text: Will's delay — it involves silver in capital

indicators.note: the capital wraps round the silver

parts.note: Rome is a capital city
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A hold-up in a will, involving silver in a capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: The misprint: delay should read deray, giving R. Will is Shakespeare; deray is old for disorder.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's word for a commotion or tumult, a variant of rummage.

clue.text: Nation guards record divined by partitions

indicators.note: the nation encloses the record

parts.note: a nation is a state
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: A country protects an album that fortune-tellers read through screens.
explanation.walkthrough: The misprint: divined should read divided, giving D.
explanation.definitionFit: In biology the term describes a structure separated into compartments by septa.

clue.text: Neuter pony roughly, without love? One remaining foal, as before

indicators.note: the remaining letters are put roughly into a new order
the zero is dropped from the words

parts.note: O is love, the nil score

explanation.surface: Castrate a pony carelessly, without affection, and one foal is left.
explanation.walkthrough: The misprint: foal should read feal, giving E. Feal is an old word for faithful; 'as before' marks the archaism.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's term for an honest, trusty fellow who stays loyal.

clue.text: Mill facing upstream, second with cant?

parts.note: to cant can mean to toss or throw with a jerk

explanation.surface: A watermill turned to face upstream is paired with a second one that tilts.
explanation.walkthrough: The misprint: Mill should read Hill, giving H. A hill's stoss side faces the direction a glacier came from.
explanation.definitionFit: In geology the stoss side of a hill or rock faces the oncoming flow of ice or water.

clue.text: To work herd, last of timber must be out on top

indicators.note: picks out the final letter of the timber word
says that last letter is moved to the front

parts.note: logs are timber

explanation.surface: Instruction to drive cattle: the end of the wood must go on top.
explanation.walkthrough: The misprint: herd should read hard, giving A.
explanation.definitionFit: To toil steadily at heavy labour is to grind away at a task.

clue.text: Two salts describing part of penal structure

parts.note: a tar is a sailor, an old salt
sal is the Latin chemical word for salt

explanation.surface: A pair of sailors writing about a section of the prison.
explanation.walkthrough: The misprint: penal should read pedal, giving D.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective relates to the bones of the ankle, part of the foot's skeleton.

clue.text: Durban fellow, dandyish youth with secrets revelled

parts.note: ou is South African slang for a man
a Ted is a Teddy boy, a 1950s dandy

explanation.surface: A man from Durban and a flashy youngster partied with their secrets.
explanation.walkthrough: The misprint: revelled should read revealed, giving A.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone exposed, especially as gay, has had their secrets made public.

clue.text: Mouse fed with bit of ricotta, one making one's mark in carinas?

definitions.text: one making one's mark in carinas?

indicators.note: the black eye takes the letter inside

parts.note: a mouse is a black eye, as is a shiner

indicators.note: only the opening letter of ricotta is used

explanation.surface: A rodent given some cheese, by someone leaving their mark on boat keels.
explanation.walkthrough: The misprint: carinas should read caritas, giving T. Members of this US fraternity are known for charity, running children's hospitals.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of this American Masonic order make their name through charitable work.

clue.text: Equivalent of dung in US river? First being removed disguises giggle

definitions.text: Equivalent of dung in US river?

indicators.note: says the opening letter of the synonym for disguises is dropped

parts.note: disguises means covers, as in conceals
a giggle is a laugh

explanation.surface: An odd question about manure in an American river, followed by someone hiding a snigger.
explanation.walkthrough: The misprint: dung should read dune, giving E. Chambers gives this word in US use as a sandbar in a river, which is a kind of underwater dune.
explanation.definitionFit: Chambers records this Dutch-derived term in America for a sandbar in a river, a submerged dune of sand.

clue.text: Make net chart for traveller, mum included

indicators.note: the word for mum is placed within the traveller's abbreviation

parts.note: a commercial traveller is a sales rep
mum is ma

explanation.surface: A request to draw a fishing-net diagram for a salesman, with mother along.
explanation.walkthrough: The misprint: net should read new, giving W.
explanation.definitionFit: To map again is to draw a fresh chart of the same ground.

clue.text: Strong draught? Jumper required

definitions.meaning: a dark, strong beer drawn on draught
misprinted for humper: one who humps loads, a carrier of luggage

explanation.walkthrough: The misprint: Jumper should read Humper, giving H; 'required' just links the second sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a heavy dark beer and a station or hotel baggage carrier.

clue.text: Set device for projecting images, including appropriate technology

indicators.note: the projector encloses the technology's letters

parts.note: an episcope projects images of opaque objects

explanation.surface: A projector kit built with suitable tech.
explanation.walkthrough: The misprint: Set should read See, giving E.
explanation.definitionFit: A bishop's see, the office or term of a bishop, is the same idea.

clue.text: Once treated with gold will jar having shilling thrown in

indicators.note: the shilling's letter is tossed inside the verb for jar

parts.note: to jar is to grate, as on the nerves
S is the old abbreviation for a shilling, a pre-decimal British coin

explanation.surface: Something formerly gilded will rattle when a coin is tossed into it.
explanation.walkthrough: The misprint: gold should read good, giving O. Spenser-era English used this as the past participle of grace.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic past participle of grace, so it describes someone favoured or treated with goodwill in older English.

clue.text: It may enhance dish of elders I love, caught in sea abroad (9, two words)

definitions.text: It may enhance dish of elders

indicators.note: says I and love sit inside the foreign sea

parts.note: mare is Latin and Italian for sea
Eros is love, the Greek god

explanation.surface: Something to improve a meal for old people: my love trapped in a foreign sea.
explanation.walkthrough: The misprint: elders should read elvers, giving V. Elvers are young eels.
explanation.definitionFit: A pink mayonnaise and ketchup sauce served with seafood such as prawns or eels.

clue.text: Such as crutches contributing to leg gymnastics

indicators.note: contributing to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Walking aids that help with exercises for the legs.
explanation.walkthrough: The misprint: crutches should read clutches, giving L. A clutch is a nest of eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: Clutches are batches of eggs laid together, so they are full of eggs.

clue.text: Arrant knight, young man in grip of anguish

indicators.note: says the youth's word sits inside the word for anguish

parts.note: anguish is pain
a lad is a young man

explanation.surface: A thoroughgoing knight, still a youth, is held by torment.
explanation.walkthrough: The misprint: Arrant should read Errant, giving E.
explanation.definitionFit: Charlemagne's twelve peers were the original knightly champions, the type of the wandering chivalrous hero.

clue.text: Blast covering the ground fast, the ache getting worse

indicators.note: says the letters of the ache are distorted into a new order

explanation.surface: Damn running so quickly: the pain is getting worse.
explanation.walkthrough: The misprint: Blast should read Beast, giving E.
explanation.definitionFit: The big cat is the fastest land animal, a beast that covers ground at speed.

clue.text: Render less peptic Isère silt after treatment

indicators.note: the river's name and silt are processed into a new order

explanation.surface: Making digestion easier with mud from the French river Isère, once it has been processed.
explanation.walkthrough: The misprint: peptic should read septic, giving S. The accent on Isère is ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: To make something free of germs is to make it less likely to turn septic.

clue.text: Rock antics, energy-filled? Coaches are included in them

indicators.note: the rearranged letters are filled with the energy symbol
to rock is to shake, so the letters of antics are shaken up

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Rock-and-roll stunts full of energy, with buses counted among them.
explanation.walkthrough: The misprint: Coaches should read Roaches, giving R.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the zoological class of insects, which includes cockroaches.

clue.text: It's comb to pass untidy nipper mostly, note, in care of old woman

indicators.note: the rearranged letters and the note are held inside the word for old woman

parts.note: hag is a disparaging word for an old woman

indicators.note: untidy says the letters of the shortened nipper are jumbled
mostly drops the final letter of nipper

explanation.surface: A grooming instruction for a scruffy child, left with an old lady.
explanation.walkthrough: The misprint: comb should read come, giving E. 'untidy' rearranges NIPPE into APPENI.
explanation.definitionFit: An event is what has come to pass, an occurrence.

clue.text: Mate repeatedly feeling like flu?

indicators.note: says the word for mate appears twice

parts.note: a mate is a pal

explanation.surface: Calling to a friend over and over while feeling under the weather.
explanation.walkthrough: The misprint: flu should read fly, giving Y. Insects feel with their palps.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective relates to palps, the sensory feelers an insect such as a fly uses to touch and taste.

clue.text: Gland's smelling — it's coated in blood

indicators.note: it sits inside the word for blood

parts.note: gore is spilt blood
the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A gland gives off an odour, being covered in blood.
explanation.walkthrough: The misprint: smelling should read swelling, giving W.
explanation.definitionFit: An enlargement of the thyroid in the neck, a gland that has swollen.

clue.text: What's in superior plantation, we hear? It's used for shopping sensation

indicators.note: says the letters are spelt as they are pronounced

parts.note: U is upper-class or superior, and sugar cane is what grows in a plantation

explanation.surface: An odd riddle about an upmarket estate, then something employed for the thrill of retail.
explanation.walkthrough: The misprint: shopping should read stopping, giving T.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a local anaesthetic, a drug used to block feeling in part of the body.

clue.text: Mob dancing in company stumping performers

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go inside the company abbreviation
dancing says the letters of mob jig into a new order

explanation.surface: A crowd dances among a firm of cricketers taking wickets.
explanation.walkthrough: The misprint: stumping should read stomping, giving O. Stumping is a cricket dismissal, which steers the surface away.
explanation.definitionFit: A small jazz or dance band, a group of musicians that plays stomping numbers.

clue.text: Chump turned over part of boot just behind the bow

definitions.text: part of boot just behind the bow

indicators.note: the word for chump is read backwards

parts.note: a chump is a fool

explanation.surface: An idiot flipped over a section of footwear behind the bow.
explanation.walkthrough: The misprint: boot should read boat, giving A.
explanation.definitionFit: A nautical term for the rounded side of a ship's bow near where the hull curves in.

clue.text: Sex? It's messing about in field

indicators.note: says the letters of field are messed into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone asks about sex: it involves fooling around in a meadow.
explanation.walkthrough: The misprint: Sex should read Rex, giving R. The Rex is a curly-coated breed of cat.
explanation.definitionFit: Any member of the cat family, of which the Rex is a domestic breed.

clue.text: English cathedral city attractive to those keen on ribbing?

definitions.text: attractive to those keen on ribbing?

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire

explanation.surface: An English cathedral town appeals to people who like teasing.
explanation.walkthrough: The misprint: ribbing should read dibbing, giving D. Dibbing is fishing by bobbing bait on the water.
explanation.definitionFit: Full of slippery fish, so appealing to anglers who fish by dapping.

clue.text: Contents of meal booked executive committee got in ready

indicators.note: the committee's letters get inside the word for ready

parts.note: ripe means ready
EC is short for executive committee

explanation.surface: Diners have reserved a meal whose committee has prepared itself.
explanation.walkthrough: The misprint: booked should read cooked, giving C.
explanation.definitionFit: A set of instructions lists the ingredients that go into a cooked dish.

clue.text: Parliamentarian in the East sorted out what makes some Japanese nosy

indicators.note: places the member's letters inside the rearranged group
says the letters of the and east are rearranged

parts.note: E is the compass abbreviation for east
MP is a member of parliament

explanation.surface: An MP in the Far East settles what makes certain Japanese people inquisitive.
explanation.walkthrough: The misprint: nosy should read nosh, giving H. 'sorted out' rearranges THEE as TEEH. Japanese stays: this fermented soya cake is Indonesian but eaten in Japan too.
explanation.definitionFit: A fermented soya-bean cake used as a food, so it makes a meal or nosh.

clue.text: Cell to appear? It's closed by state briefly

indicators.note: says it is enclosed by the shortened state

parts.note: Cal is short for California
the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A prison cell turning up, shut in by a state.
explanation.walkthrough: The misprint: Cell should read Call, giving A. The word is an old form of citation, a summons.
explanation.definitionFit: An obsolete word for a citation or summons to court.

clue.text: Rattling sabre, alert, one filed bolts

indicators.note: rattling says the letters of sabre and alert are shaken up

explanation.surface: A soldier rattles a sword on guard, then one runs off in line.
explanation.walkthrough: The misprint: filed should read fired, giving R.
explanation.definitionFit: A crossbowman, a soldier who shot crossbow bolts.

clue.text: Sanctimonious about love, Jock's taking cure

indicators.note: the pious word wraps round the zero

parts.note: sanctimonious means holy, as in holier-than-thou
O is love, a nil score in tennis

explanation.surface: A pious person enfolding love as a Scotsman seeks healing.
explanation.walkthrough: The misprint: cure should read care, giving A. Jock is the crossword's Scotsman, flagging a Scottish word.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scots the word means cautious or gentle, describing someone going carefully.

clue.text: Regular feature of rooks, origin being about a loch

indicators.note: the word for origin goes round the loch

parts.note: a seed is an origin
Loch Awe is a Scottish loch

explanation.surface: Rooks regularly show up where things began, around a Scottish lake.
explanation.walkthrough: The misprint: rooks should read rocks, giving C.
explanation.definitionFit: Marine algae such as wrack are a regular sight clinging to rocks on the shore.
